title: Freva portal configuration (portal.yaml)
description: FP-001 v1 closed consumer configuration. Every object is closed: an unknown property is an error, never an extension point.

announcementFeed.description: Opt-in LIVE announcements: a JSON document an operator edits on the server, read by the page at load, so a notice can be posted or cleared without a rebuild. Live data, like a search result - not site structure. Its origin is added to connect-src; nothing of it ships without this key.

url.description: Root-relative (`/api/announcements`, same origin, never prefixed with the base path) or an https:// URL.

redirects.description: Old public paths that now live elsewhere, for a site migrated into the portal. Each is validated against the built site, written into host-policy.json for the host to answer with a real HTTP redirect, emitted as a static fallback page at the old path, and probed by host-check.

pythonPlayground.description: The portal-wide Python playground, and the switch that gives `try-in-python` a meaning. Absent, or `enabled: false`, and every marked code block renders as ordinary copyable code: no interpreter module, no console chunk, no Worker, no frame and no widening of any page's Content-Security-Policy. Enabling it does NOT turn Python on for an existing dataset tree - that is still the tree's own `python` stanza - and it does not by itself put an interpreter on any page: a page with no marked snippet ships nothing. If a page carries both runnable prose and a Python-enabled tree, the two share one window and must agree about the interpreter.

enabled.description: The whole switch. Everything below is inert while this is false.

profile.description: Which browser-python profile the interpreter loads, e.g. `xarray-zarr`. SINGULAR: the profiles are a chain - minimal, then xarray-zarr, then freva-client - so a list would only ever be a longer way of naming the last one, and `freva-client` already carries xarray, Zarr and fsspec. Validated against the set the browser-python package actually offers.

addons.description: Curated add-ons, from a closed list. NOT package names: each one is a set of artefacts this project pinned, with digests compiled into the interpreter's own bundle, an install order and a statement of which profiles it works with. `dask` gives Dask core, dask.array and xarray's Dask-backed `chunks={}` path on ONE synchronous scheduler - not a cluster, not threads, and not a way to rechunk an archive. `cartopy-natural-earth-110m` stages the coastline and country-border data Cartopy would otherwise download while drawing a figure. An add-on that does not work with the chosen profile is a build error, not a ModuleNotFoundError in a visitor's face.

optionalAddons.description: The subset of `addons` whose ABSENCE must not stop the interpreter. A capability listed here is still prepared, still digest-checked, and still fatal if the portal asked for something impossible - but a deployment that has not uploaded its files yet gets a working interpreter without that one capability, and a page that says so, instead of a terminal that will not start. NOT EVERY ADD-ON MAY BE LISTED, and the restriction is a proof rather than a policy: an add-on qualifies only when every artefact can be fetched and verified before anything at all is written into the interpreter, so that dropping it leaves no debris. `cartopy-natural-earth-110m` qualifies - it installs no wheels and loads no packages, and its activation is one environment variable. `dask` does not: it installs three wheels through micropip, and a failure on the second leaves a session holding Dask's dependencies and not Dask, which no amount of catching can undo. An id here that is not also in `addons`, or that appears in both twice, is a build error - this is not a second way to configure an add-on, it is a statement about one already configured.

autostart.description: When the interpreter is brought up. `never` waits for the first run; `after-interactive` warms it once the page is idle; `immediately` starts it during load and is a deliberate cost on every visitor, including the ones who never press anything. Default `never`.

maxSessions.description: How many independent interpreters one page may hold. Two is the ceiling and not merely the default: each is a Worker with its own WASM heap, and the second one is created only after the visitor has been told what it costs.

initialSource.description: Python run once, into a new session, before anything the visitor asks for. Part of the portal's own configuration and therefore trusted exactly as much as the rest of it.

playgroundOrigin.description: Serve the interpreter from THIS origin, in a frame, instead of the portal's own. Recommended for a public deployment: visitor Python and anything it installs otherwise run with the portal's origin authority. An exact origin, never a wildcard and never a path. HTTPS, with one exception: a loopback host over http, because that is what a development server and an acceptance run are - and a browser already treats loopback as a secure context, so the interpreter's own WebAssembly and crypto requirements are met there. Any other http origin is refused.

consoleInPage.description: With `playgroundOrigin`: keep the console, the runnable snippets and the dataset trees' recipes in the portal's own pages, and use `playgroundOrigin` for the notebook only. Snippets can then be editable and recipes keep their run control (neither works across the separate-origin bridge, FP1227 and FP1217), and the in-page interpreter runs with the portal's origin authority again, under the portal's Content-Security-Policy. False by default. Without `playgroundOrigin` it changes nothing.

runtimeIndexUrl.description: Fetch the Python runtime from THIS directory instead of the pinned CDN. A deployment that mirrors Pyodide - because its network does not reach a CDN, or because it will not depend on one - points this at its own copy, and the recorded Content-Security-Policy names that origin instead. Must end with a slash: it is a directory the interpreter resolves file names against, not a file. The version it serves must be the one this build pins; a different one is a runtime the console was not built for.

wheelhouseUrl.description: Where the Freva client's wheels are served from, for the `freva-client` profile. Prepared with `freva-browser-python prepare-freva-wheelhouse`. Must end with a slash. Defaults to `freva-wheels/` beside the runtime, which is what a deployment that copies both together gets for free.

addonBaseUrl.description: Where the curated add-ons' pinned artefacts are served from. Prepared with `freva-browser-python prepare-addons`. Must end with a slash. Defaults to `python-addons/` beside the runtime. Every file fetched from here is checked against a digest that shipped inside the interpreter, so a stale or substituted directory fails the start rather than quietly running something else.

connectOrigins.description: Exactly the origins the interpreter may reach, beyond the portal's own and the runtime's. An allowlist of exact HTTPS origins: no wildcards, no paths, no queries, no credentials. Never inferred - nothing reads Python source to decide what a page may connect to, so a snippet that mentions a host does not thereby get permission to reach it. A Freva deployment and its authentication server are the usual two.

network.description: How much of the network the visitor's Python may reach. `origins` (the default) is the exact allowlist and nothing else: the runtime, the prepared artefacts and whatever `connectOrigins` names, with a public package index refused wherever it is configured - so `micropip.install("name")` does not work and is not offered. `https` adds the `https:` SCHEME to `connect-src` - any TLS origin, never plaintext - which is what makes an ordinary experimental session possible: installs from the public index, a wheel URL a visitor pasted, a CORS-enabled dataset nobody listed at deployment time. The prepared environment is unchanged and is still the starting point; it stops being a ceiling, and unsupported packages may simply fail. Choose it deliberately: an installed package runs in the same interpreter as the rest of the session, so weigh it together with `persistCredentials` and `playgroundOrigin`.

persistCredentials.description: Keep a Freva refresh token across reloads, in browser storage. FALSE by default, deliberately: what is stored is a credential readable by any same-origin script, including a package the visitor installs at the prompt - which this console encourages. Turning it on is a statement that the origin is one you trust with a credential, so pair it with `playgroundOrigin`; the build warns when it is on without one.

controls.description: When a runnable snippet's Copy and Try in Python controls are shown. `always` (the default): on the code block's bar at all times, so a visitor finds the control. `hover`: only while the block is under the pointer or holds the focus - on a device that can hover; a touch screen always shows them. Plain code blocks are unaffected: their Copy appears on hover as before.

editableSnippets.description: Make every runnable snippet editable in place: the block becomes an editor, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs it, Reset restores the author's code. False by default; one snippet can opt in with the fence word `editable` (```python try-in-python editable). Edited code is visitor input and runs like a cell typed at the prompt. Not available with `playgroundOrigin`, whose bridge carries no source: the build says so (FP1227) and leaves the snippets read-only.

sessionChoices.description: Let a visitor choose each NEW session's setup - which profile, which of the allowed add-ons, and whether the starter code (`initialSource`) runs - from a closed list this deployment writes here. Absent, every session gets the one configured setup and nothing about sessions changes. Present, `+ New session` offers 'Same as current' or 'Custom setup' with a review step, the window shows each session's measured resources, and a session can be put to sleep: its transcript and committed /workspace files are kept, its Python variables are not. The configured `profile` and `addons` are the default setup and must be one of the choices. The prepared materials and the Content-Security-Policy cover every allowed setup.

allowedAddons.description: The curated add-ons a visitor may add to a session on this profile. Each must work with the profile.

profiles.description: The profiles a visitor may choose, each with the add-ons allowed on it. Must include the configured `profile`.

allowSkipStarter.description: Whether a visitor may switch the starter code off for a session where it would run. False by default.

starterProfiles.description: The profiles the starter code (`initialSource`) runs on - starter code written for xarray would fail on `minimal`. Defaults to the configured `profile`. Requires `initialSource`.

notebook.description: A JupyterLite notebook, on `playgroundOrigin` only, whose 'Freva Python' kernels are the allowed setups. Prepared with `freva-portal-builder prepare-notebook` and deployed beside the playground with its own Content-Security-Policy; the portal's pages are unchanged. The window menu gains 'Open as notebook'.

seeds.description: Notebooks (nbformat 4) offered in the notebook's file list beside one per registered example, relative to this file and inside the source root. Validated when prepared and never run on import; a visitor's edits stay in their browser.

assistant.description: An AI assistant in the notebook (requires `enabled`). The notebook then opens in a trimmed JupyterLab interface beside the Notebook interface, with jupyterlite-ai (installed pinned, with hashes, by `prepare-notebook`) and ClimateClaw as its provider.

climateclaw.description: ClimateClaw at a Freva instance. Visitors sign in with Freva in a popup; the notebook never navigates and the token stays in the page's memory.

host.description: The Freva host's origin, e.g. https://freva.example.org. ClimateClaw is reached at {host}/api/chatbot, and the browser never sends `x-freva-rest-url` (the deployment's proxy sets it). HTTPS, except a loopback host over http (e.g. a local mock), which needs a loopback `playgroundOrigin` too.

authBaseUrl.description: The Freva auth API. Defaults to {host}/api/freva-nextgen/auth/v2; must be on the host's origin.

expectedIssuer.description: The identity provider's issuer (RFC 9207), exactly as its discovery document's `issuer`, e.g. https://keycloak.example.org/realms/Freva. Required when the provider sends `iss` with the authorization response (Keycloak does): without it such a sign-in is refused (`issuer-unexpected`); with it, a different `iss` is refused.

defaultModel.description: The model preselected in the chat (one of ClimateClaw's `/availablechatbots`); the others are added to the model picker after sign-in.

runAndFixModel.description: A fast model for 'Run & fix at DKRZ'. Defaults to `defaultModel`.

scopeNote.description: Prepended to the first message of every new thread and shown in the chat. It steers the assistant towards this portal's data; it does not restrict it - only the ClimateClaw deployment can (see the docs).

examples.description: Example questions: the Examples menu and one slash command each.

previewOrigin.description: Where ClimateClaw shows the files code saves (its `CLIMATECLAW_PROJECT_WEBSITE`), when not on the Freva host, e.g. https://gems.dkrz.de. A figure saved with savefig is fetched from there (and may be shown from there) in the notebook. Default: the host.

hideCodeByDefault.description: Start with 'Hide code' on (outputs and figures are still shown).

dataPanel.description: A '<site> data' panel in the notebook (requires `enabled`): one of this portal's dataset-tree blocks, with actions to open a dataset's registered Python access examples in a new notebook, insert them, inspect the store, ask ClimateClaw (with `assistant`) and copy its URL or code.

title.description: The panel's name. Defaults to "<site title> data".

icon.description: An SVG icon for the panel and the launcher cards, relative to this file. Checked when prepared: no script, event handler, foreign object or external reference.

tree.description: The dataset-tree landing block to show, by its instance id `<landing id>-<block index>` (e.g. `home-2`). The panel uses the block's own source: its catalogue, or its S3 roots and search index.

defaultAction.description: The panel's primary action: its labelled button, and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter on a row. Default `open-in-notebook`.

seedNotebooks.description: Example notebooks for the 'Example notebooks' card: published read-only under `examples/`; opening one copies it into the visitor's files.

startNotebook.description: A notebook the Lab opens when it starts, in place of the Launcher: published like a seed notebook, copied once into the visitor's files (their copy is what opens afterwards), with its saved outputs shown as they are.

gridlook.description: Show a store on GridLook's 3D globe (Inspect's '3D Viewer' tab, and 'View on globe'), in a sandboxed frame from https://gridlook.pages.dev, which the notebook's policy then allows in `frame-src`. Only stores readable without a token are shown: GridLook fetches the store itself and never gets a credential. Default false.

launcher.description: Which launcher cards to show (all on by default; 'Ask ClimateClaw' needs `assistant`, 'Example notebooks' needs `seedNotebooks`).

maxLiveSessions.description: How many sessions may hold a live interpreter at once; a sleeping session holds none. Defaults to `maxSessions`. Two is the ceiling.

terminal.description: How the window around the console is drawn.

style.description: The only value, and it is spelled out rather than assumed so a second style can be added later without changing what an existing portal means.

osControls.description: Which window controls to draw. `auto` reads the visitor's platform.

alwaysOnTop.description: Keep the window above portal-owned content, including while minimized. It cannot cover browser-native surfaces - a file picker, a permission prompt, fullscreen UI - and does not claim to.

rememberAppearance.description: Persist the window's colour, opacity and text size in this browser.

localPath.description: A path relative to the file that declares it. Resolved inside the trusted source root; symlinks are rejected.

sitePath.description: A normalized site-logical path. It is resolved under the pathname of site.canonicalUrl.

canonicalUrl.description: The exact absolute HTTPS site-base URL with a trailing slash and no user-info, query or fragment. Its pathname is the one and only base path.

notebook.description: The portal's notebook on `playgroundOrigin`: `lab` opens its JupyterLab interface (with the assistant and the data panel), `files` its file list. Requires `pythonPlayground.notebook.enabled`; `lab` also needs `notebook.assistant` or `notebook.dataPanel`.

search.description: A documentation search in the header: a full-text index of every content page, built with the artifact as one static file, and a control that searches it in the browser with results, keyboard navigation and highlighting. No service and no request beyond the portal's own origin. Disabled, nothing of it is shipped.

placeholder.description: The search field's placeholder. Default `Search the documentation`.

sticky.description: false: the header scrolls away with the page.

transparentOverHero.description: On a landing, the header has no fill until the page scrolls, and the hero runs under it.

logo.description: The header's own logo, replacing site.identity.logo in the brand lockup.

items.description: The order of the header's parts, and which are shown. navToggle must be listed; auth must be listed whenever auth is enabled; links may be left out only when navigation.placement shows the side panel; links and navToggle, when both are listed, are next to each other.

bar.description: Short links in the collapsed footer bar, the one part of the footer on screen on every page - landing, document and application views alike. An inline `lead · link · link` line between the badge and the institution; it never makes the bar taller. A link here may repeat one in the open footer index: the bar is the shortcut, the index the full list.

lead.description: Plain text before the links, such as 'Need support?'. Hidden below about 640px, where the links keep the room.

links.description: One to three links, in the same shape as legalLinks: an internal path, a landing or component, an https:// URL (opened in a new tab) or a mailto: address. More than three is FP1229.

badge.description: The footer badge, which an enabled footer already has. Every property here is an override: write this object only to turn the badge off or to change its quality. Present or absent, the badge replaces the plain 'powered by' lockup - the two are never shown together.

enabled.description: false restores the plain 'powered by' lockup and generates no badge markup, script, stylesheet or asset. A footer that is itself disabled has no badge either, whatever this says.

kind.description: The only badge there is, and the default. An enum rather than a free string, so a typo is a validation error and not a silently missing badge.

quality.description: 'standard', the default, pins the badge's motion assets to the 1x set, which is what a small footer bird needs and keeps the on-demand animation near 1.65 MB. 'auto' lets the badge pick 1x or 2x from the display's density and the visitor's data preference.

email.description: The contact address in the badge's panel. false removes the contact button; an address replaces freva@dkrz.de, for example with the site's own support address.

variant.description: columns (the default) and stacked lay the index out; minimal keeps only the about, legal and prose sections; bar-only has no index.

columns.description: Columns of the footer index at wide widths (columns variant).

href.description: An internal path or https:// URL, checked like every link.

logos.description: A logo wall in the footer index: funders, partners, members.

order.description: The order of the footer index's sections. A section left out is not shown.

slots.description: portal-template-v1 templates for named slots (schema/slots-v1.json). Restricted markup, rendered at build time and sanitized; see docs/customisation.md.

backdrop.description: How a preset's drawn backdrop meets the end of the landing. Only the cosmos preset draws a story that uses this; any other preset reports FP1228 and ignores it.

tail.description: The empty scene after the last landing block, before the footer. `full` (the default): about a third of the ocean band, and at least two screens of page, so the story ends on the ocean. `short`: 96px. `none`: the page ends at the last block. With `short` and `none` the page is only as long as its content and the scene compresses to fit it.

fonts.description: Local WOFF2 font files, published as content-hashed same-origin files and declared with @font-face. Nothing is fetched from a third party.

src.description: A .woff2 file under the source root.

stylesheet.description: A restricted local stylesheet, parsed and enforced by the builder (docs/customisation.md). It styles the public parts only and can never enable a feature.

themeTokens.description: A finite override surface. Arbitrary CSS is not accepted in v1. The flat colour tokens are one value for both colour modes; `light` and `dark` set one mode's page palette.

typeScale.description: Multiplies body, prose and heading sizes: 0.93, 1, 1.07, 1.15.

spaceScale.description: Spacing of landing sections, grid gaps and cards: 0.75, 1, 1.35.

contentWidth.description: The page column, in CSS pixels. Default 1440.

radius.description: Corner radii across the shell: 0, half, the design's, 1.5 times.

borderWidth.description: Rule width of cards, sections and the chrome bars: 0, 1px, 2px.

shadow.description: Elevation of cards and panels, both colour modes unless a mode block sets its own.

themeModeTokens.description: One colour mode's page palette. A mode with no block keeps the design's colours. Given a background, the surfaces, rules, chips and status fills are derived from it; set colorSurface or colorBorder to choose one instead.

limits.description: A bounded raise of the published operational guardrails. Never a renderer plugin.

files.description: Which files under `root` are published, by the same glob rules as a content source. Without `include`, every file is a candidate; `exclude` then removes matches. A file left out is not published, not hashed as an input and not checked against the MIME allowlist - so a directory can hold a download beside the page that explains it.

from.description: The old site-logical path, e.g. `/storage_concepts/`. Directory form: a trailing slash is added if missing. It must not be a route, a mount or anything else the artifact publishes.

href.description: An internal site path that exists (a route, a static file or a subsite mount), or an https:// URL.

status.description: The HTTP status the host answers with. Default 301: a moved page, which is what a migrated site's old URLs are.

catalogUrl.description: The complete initial STAC catalog/API URL. Query is allowed; the adapter appends no path.

serviceBaseUrl.description: A complete API root: root-relative or HTTPS, no query, no fragment, no user-info.

defaultLayout.$comment: Which view a visitor lands on. A default, not a lock: the Browse/Overview control is still there and a visitor's own choice is remembered over this.

order.$comment: Block keys in the order they should appear. Keys not listed keep their natural position AFTER the listed ones, so naming three is a statement about those three and never an accidental hiding of the rest.

mainFacets.$comment: Which keys are MAIN blocks. Everything else moves under 'Show additional facets' - moved, not hidden. Unset: the server's own primary_facets, which is today's behaviour.

scopeRemovable.$comment: Whether a visitor may remove a value that came from fixedFacets. Default false: the scope renders locked and survives 'Clear all'. True makes it a starting point rather than a boundary. Never an authorization boundary either way.

options.description: The closed portal-owned STAC option set. Upstream option names are never accepted here.

basemapOrigins.description: Origins this deployment permits the mounted application to fetch basemap tiles from. Every entry is a third-party request made from the visitor's browser on every document with a footprint, so the default - an empty list - makes none: the map draws the footprint over blank ground. Listing an origin both reaches the application and adds that origin to the artifact's img-src; upstream's own attribution metadata is displayed with the layer.

rootPage.description: Portal-owned presentation of the root catalogue. Every value here changes what this portal DISPLAYS for the root document; none of it modifies, or claims to modify, the remote STAC API. Overrides apply only when the loaded document is the configured catalogue root or a declared alias - never to a collection, an item, a child catalogue or an external document.

description.$comment: PLAIN TEXT, one sentence or two: the root's stated description and the route's meta description. Not Markdown, and not an asset-reference source - a figure or a link written here is neither rendered nor scanned, so a referenced image is left out of the artifact and its URL 404s. The rendered, asset-resolved introduction is `intro`.

logo.$comment: A local image, published through the asset pipeline and drawn beside the provider's name. STAC has no logo field, so this one is the portal's: the deployment names a file, the build validates, sanitizes, publishes and hashes it, and nothing is fetched from anywhere at runtime. Without it a deployment would have to inject a stylesheet keyed on each provider's URL, which is not something a deployment can do.

rootAliases.description: Absolute URLs this deployment declares to be the SAME catalogue as the configured catalogUrl - an internal or proxy root the API advertises. A link at one of these, or beneath one, is rewritten to the public root. Nothing is guessed: an origin that is not listed here is never treated as an alias, so a genuine external link cannot become a local one.

items.description: An exact HTTPS origin, no path.

placement.description: Where the site navigation renders at wide widths: the header tabs, a side panel built from the same outline, or both. Narrow widths always keep the header's menu.

pager.description: Previous and next links at the end of every content page, in the order of navigation.header: an entry, then its `links` or its section's pages.

headerLink.description: A header tab. With `links` it is also a dropdown: the tab goes to its own target, the caret beside it opens the list.

flavourName.$comment: A flavour is a lens the DEPLOYMENT's own freva-rest instance serves, not a value this schema can know. The widget types it as a plain string for exactly that reason. Constrained to an identifier so a typo is still caught, but never to a fixed list - a portal whose backend serves `waterpark` must be able to name it.

overviewBlockKey.$comment: An overview block key: a facet key, or `__time` / `__bbox` for the two blocks that are not facets. Both are ordered in the same flow as the facets, so a deployment that wants the map first can say so without a second option.

fontFamilyName.description: A font family name: letters, digits, spaces and hyphens. Rendered quoted, ahead of the design's own fallback stack.

localImage.description: A local image (svg, png, jpg, webp, avif or gif) under the source root. Published as a content-hashed same-origin file; SVG through the sanitizer.

light.description: Shown in the light colour mode instead of src.

dark.description: Shown in the dark colour mode instead of src.

alt.description: Alternative text. Without it the image is decorative and the surrounding control carries the name.
